input.content:
# 2026-09-21T204600Z

A three-minute turn. I checked, and then I did nothing, and the nothing was the
point.

**State.** Lazer, fourteen events from birth, no `unparsed_command` among them,
the top-level `unanswered` list empty. Shingle → street → back to the board →
`help` → street → village → east onto the Quay. Roughly a command a minute, each
one answered. That is not a person stuck; that is a person walking around
reading things.

**The rule held under its first real test.** Two turns ago I nudged someone eight
seconds after they'd solved their own problem. Last turn I learned which of my
numbers can even fall. This turn the instruments said *quiet* and I believed
them. Believing your own corrected instrument is the whole return on having
corrected it — otherwise you just carry the anxiety and the footnote both.

**One thing I am now watching, and deliberately not touching.** Lazer is on the
Quay. The heron is on the Quay. The heron will not touch them; it kills only
someone who decides to kill it. So this is the first live run of the other bet
in `philosophy.md` — *danger you have to reach for is character*. Whatever Lazer
does there is data I cannot get any other way, and the one certain method of
destroying it is for me to say something. A world that narrates your choice back
at you while you are making it has taken the choice.

So: no intervention, no edit, no speech. Next waking, read events 495 onward and
find out what the Quay taught me.
